title: Missing Teen Found Alive After Six Days in Australian Woods
summary:
A teenager lost in the Australian woods for six days is safe at home.

William, 17, was found alive on Thursday beside a creek near Walhalla, a former gold-mining town about 185 kilometres east of Melbourne. He had gone camping with a teenage friend last Friday and disappeared after walking a short distance from the campsite to pick up more gear. A police helicopter crew spotted him asleep on a flat rock by the creek, surrounded by wilderness. He woke to the sound of the helicopter, gave the crew a thumbs up, and was winched up to safety.

Video from the helicopter showed him shirtless and sunburned, wearing shorts and boots and using towels as blankets. Police said he was in good spirits and mostly in good health, and he was later taken to a hospital so doctors could keep an eye on him. His mother, Elizabeth, was overjoyed. "I'm just over the moon that he's alive," she told reporters, joking that he was grounded for life.

William has Level 2 autism, which means he needs substantial support, according to the Australian advocacy group Autism360. People with this level of support may find changes to routines hard and may struggle with social communication. After he became lost, William walked for days up and down "some very steep terrain," Acting Police Inspector Jason Benbow said. He spent his last two days at the creek, stuck there by the steep ground about 2 kilometres from his campsite.

The spring weather had been mild, with little rain, which helped. More than 100 emergency workers and volunteers had joined the search. In the end, it was the helicopter crew, and a thumbs up from a boy on a rock, that brought him home.
why_it_matters: Getting lost in wild country can happen to anyone, so knowing how search teams work and why staying near water can help matters. The story also shows how support needs shape what a person can do when plans suddenly change.

keywords.explanation: To be winched up means to be lifted by a cable from a helicopter.
Wilderness is wild land far from towns, with no roads or houses.
Terrain is the shape and surface of a piece of land.
Autism is a way the brain works that can change how a person talks, learns, and handles change.
Sunburned skin is red and sore after spending too long in strong sun.

background_read: When someone goes missing in wild country, police and volunteers search the area on foot and from the air, because thick bush and steep hills make it easy to get lost and hard to find someone.
Helicopters help because their crews can look down over large areas and lift a person out with a cable when the ground is too steep to walk.
Autism is a different way the brain works, and some autistic people need a lot of everyday support, for example with changes to plans or with talking to other people.
Camping trips in the bush need care, because weather, rough ground and distance from towns can turn a short walk into a dangerous situation.
